label: GO step after a common a1->S1 trial went unrewarded, late in the episode
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (99% of mass; never at D2, rarely at D1), and essentially only when the previous trial was unrewarded (99% of mass has prev_reward == 0). Within that it is specific to the previous trial being a1 with a common transition to S1 (prev_action == 1: 82% of mass; prev_action == 2 only 2%; prev_common == 0 only 2%). So it is a lose-after-a1->S1 signal at the choice step. It is also strongly gated by time in episode: silent before trial ~35, and the rate climbs from trial 40 to trial 90. The predicate uses only observed history, no future variables. Dev F1 is 0.70 and mass recall 0.82. Most missed mass is at the window first trial (rel -3), where the previous trial is outside the window so prev_action is unknown. Activation looks the same there, so recall is capped by the data format, not by the feature. Most remaining false positives are cases where the agent then switches to a2. Adding action == 1 (agent stays with a1, which is model-free-like after a common loss) raises precision to 0.82 but lowers mass recall to 0.70, so it is not included. Magnitude is higher at lower model value (zero mass above value 7.73) and with policy logit favouring a1 (choice 2.8-8).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S1 u, a2 S1 u, ?; D1: a2 S1 r, a2 S1 u) and trial before (GO: a2 S1 r, a1 S1 r, a1 S2 r; D1: a2 S1 u, ?); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=8, phase=GO & ep_dec=7, phase=GO & ep_dec=9.
